g10-history-uh6-t1.overview: Major Administrative Reforms and Socio-Economic Conditions in the Post-Liberation Period sits inside Ethiopia: Internal Developments and External Influences from 1941 to 1991. Ethiopian revolution and reform shaped the years from 1941 to 1991, the focus of Unit 6 of Grade 10 History in the Ethiopian (FDRE Ministry of Education) curriculum. First, it covers post-liberation reforms and British and American influence. Then it traces early opposition from peasants, the 1960 coup, and students. Next, it explains the Ethiopian revolution of 1974 and the fall of the monarchy. Also it follows the Derg, its reforms, and the Red Terror. Finally, it looks at the Ethio-Somalia war, the question of Eritrea, and the fall of the Derg. Students will also learn how popular movements apply to real-life situations, such as calls for land and justice today.
objectives: Explain British and American influence in post-liberation Ethiopia.
Compare the land policies of the imperial and the Derg regimes.
Describe the early opposition movements against imperial rule.

Trace the Ethio-Somalia war and the question of Eritrea.
g10-history-uh6-t1.simple:
Major Administrative Reforms and Socio-Economic Conditions in the Post-Liberation Period in plain words. The exam wants you to recognise the core ideas, not to memorise whole paragraphs. Focus on:
  • First, the British era and the Anglo-Ethiopian treaties of 1942 and 1944.
  • The American era, the Point Four Agreement, and the Kagnew station.
  • Also the 1955 constitution, the twelve provinces, and land tenure such as gult and rist.
  • Development plans in trade, industry, education, and health.
